{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The black doorway opened a hand’s width.

A draft crossed the kitchen, smelling of rain and something sweet Mara couldn’t name. The scarf’s fringe lifted from the table, though the windows were shut.

Her mother pulled her hand back. “It knows what you chose.”

“Does it know why?”

“That’s for you to tell it.”

Mara stepped toward the doorway. Her mother stayed by the table, the red wool still looped around one finger. In the dark beyond the threshold, a narrow staircase descended. At the bottom, a small light trembled.

Mara tucked the cold stone into her pocket. “You said I could take one thing.”

“I said you could carry one thing.”

“That isn’t the same.”

“No,” her mother said. “It isn’t.”

Mara looked back at the scarf. For a heartbeat, she saw it around another person’s neck: a girl with rain-dark hair, standing beneath a streetlamp. The girl lifted one hand, and Mara felt an ache so sharp it seemed to have been waiting inside her all along.

“Who was she?” Mara asked.

Her mother’s eyes shone. “Your sister.”

The word settled between them, heavier than the jar. Mara gripped the doorframe. She had no memory of a sister, only an empty place at the table and the strange certainty that it had always belonged to someone.

From below came a voice, thin as a thread.

“Mara?”

Her mother closed her eyes.

Mara descended one step. The kitchen light stretched behind her, warm and yellow. In her pocket, the stone began to ring.

She went down another step.

This time, her mother followed."}
